passage.text: Nam is visiting her grandfather, and they're looking at old photos of Bangkok.
passage.reading: ˈnɑːm ɪz ˈvɪzɪtɪŋ hɜːr ˈɡrænfɑːðər, ənd ðɛr ˈlʊkɪŋ ət ˈoʊld ˈfoʊtoʊz əv ˈbæŋkɑːk.

passage.text: "Bangkok has changed a lot," her grandfather says.
passage.reading: ˈbæŋkɑːk hæz ˈtʃeɪndʒd ə ˈlɑːt, hɜːr ˈɡrænfɑːðər ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "When I was young, there used to be canals everywhere, and people traveled by boat."
passage.reading: wɛn aɪ wʌz ˈjʌŋ, ðɛr ˈjuːst tə bi kəˈnælz ˈɛvriwɛr, ənd ˈpiːpəl ˈtrævəld baɪ ˈboʊt.

passage.text: "There weren't many cars, so there wasn't much traffic.
passage.reading: ðɛr ˈwɜːrnt ˈmɛni ˈkɑːrz, soʊ ðɛr ˈwʌzənt ˈmʌtʃ ˈtræfɪk.

passage.text: Then the city developed very quickly.
passage.reading: ˈðɛn ðə ˈsɪti dɪˈvɛləpt ˈvɛri ˈkwɪkli.

passage.text: They built highways and skyscrapers, and Bangkok expanded into the rice fields."
passage.reading: ðeɪ ˈbɪlt ˈhaɪweɪz ənd ˈskaɪskreɪpərz, ənd ˈbæŋkɑːk ɪkˈspændɪd ˈɪntuː ðə ˈraɪs ˌfiːldz.
ɪz ˈɛvriθɪŋ ˈbɛtər ˈnaʊ? ˈnɑːm ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "Some things are better," her grandfather says.
passage.reading: sʌm ˈθɪŋz ər ˈbɛtər, hɜːr ˈɡrænfɑːðər ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "The trains are fast and comfortable, and the hospitals are much better.
passage.reading: ðə ˈtreɪnz ər ˈfæst ənd ˈkʌmftərbəl, ənd ðə ˈhɑːspɪtəlz ər ˈmʌtʃ ˈbɛtər.

passage.text: But the traffic is terrible, and the canals are much dirtier now."
passage.reading: bʌt ðə ˈtræfɪk ɪz ˈtɛrəbəl, ənd ðə kəˈnælz ər ˈmʌtʃ ˈdɜːrtiər ˈnaʊ.

passage.text: "Then let's take the train to the old town today," Nam says.
passage.reading: ˈðɛn ˈlɛts ˈteɪk ðə ˈtreɪn tə ði ˈoʊld ˈtaʊn təˈdeɪ, ˈnɑːm ˈsɛz.
